summary: Central process ownership improves governance while introducing a critical service, distributed-systems complexity, and pressure to over-model uncertain work.

points.text: The actor and its state store become availability and throughput dependencies. Partitioning by process ID, durable queues, and recovery testing are required before calling the design resilient.

Leases, fencing, idempotency, outbox delivery, duplicate callbacks, and compensation are difficult to implement correctly. A nominal state machine without those protocols can create stronger false confidence than a simpler workflow.

External systems may not support idempotency or transactions with the actor's store. A crash between an effect and its recorded completion can still produce duplicate payments, messages, or deployments.
Exploratory knowledge work does not always fit a predefined graph. Excessive state and verdict granularity can make process evolution slow and drive users to bypass the governed path.
